changes.evidence: X-Men: The Animated Series, 'No Mutant Is an Island': grieving Jean, Scott quits the X-Men (strips off his uniform and throws it at Xavier's feet), goes back to his childhood orphanage, and at the end of the episode returns to the X-Men. The quit and the return have no stage. ADD left 'X-Men: The Animated Series'.

Three misses, all in X-Men: The Animated Series. (1) 'Cold Vengeance': bitter over Jean and distrusting Xavier, Logan decides to leave the X-Men and goes to the Arctic; at the end he accepts he must return to the X-Men. (2) 'Lotus and the Steel': losing control, Wolverine quits the X-Men and goes back to rural Japan, then returns. (3) 'Weapon X, Lies, and Video Tape' / 'Repo Man': Weapon X captured Logan, Sabretooth, Maverick and Silver Fox, used false memory implants to make them compliant and had them carry out covert missions (forced service in the named 'Weapon X' program; Marvel Database lists Weapon X as a former affiliation). ADD left 'X-Men: The Animated Series' for the two quits. If the owner treats Weapon X as the same thing as Team X here, drop only the Weapon X stage and keep the rest.

X-Men '97 S1 episode 5 ('Remember It'): Genosha's council offers Magneto the chancellorship, he accepts on condition that Rogue also sits on the council, and she accepts the seat. After the Sentinel massacre she is back with the X-Men (episode 7: the X-Men hold Gambit's funeral and pick Rogue up on the way to Madripoor). The Genosha stage and the return to the X-Men are missing. (Her joining Magneto on Asteroid M in episode 9 is raised separately as an owner call.)

Past group left out: Warren was one of the founding X-Men. X-Men: The Animated Series 'Sanctuary' shows him in flashbacks with the first X-Men, and X-Men '97 S1 episode 1 ('To Me, My X-Men') confirms him as part of the original team (Marvel Database: 'one of the founding members of the X-Men'; 'After leaving the X-Men, Angel desperately wanted to be rid of his mutation'). The left title stays.

Past group left out: Lorna was an early X-Man with Iceman. They left the team after she nearly died on a mission, then she joined X-Factor (X-Men: The Animated Series, 'Cold Comfort'). X-Men '97 S2 episode 2 ('A Force to Be Reckoned With') again names Polaris as someone 'who used to be a member of the X-Men', and in S2 episode 6 her 'former teammates' welcome her back.

Past group left out: young Nathan is raised by Mother Askani's clan in 3960 A.D. (X-Men '97 S1 episode 10 shows Scott and Jean finding Mother Askani with the young Nathan; S2 episode 1 'Days of Past Future': Mother Askani has told Nathan he is destined to kill Apocalypse and brought the X-Men through time to train him). Marvel Database lists Clan Askani as his affiliation. The dataset's own name for the group is 'The Askani' (Mother Askani's record).

owner_calls.question: In X-Men: The Animated Series 'Old Soldiers' (World War II flashback), Logan is a Canadian soldier/agent sent with Captain America by Captain Sawyer to rescue Andre Cocteau. Should a past wartime group be added before Team X, and under what name?
options: Add another name if the episode says one
Leave as is (the screen never names his unit)
owner_calls.evidence: Marvel Database lists 'OSS (Office of Strategic Services)' as a former affiliation, citing this episode. The episode synopsis only says 'Logan of Canada', so I could not confirm that the name is said on screen.

owner_calls.question: In X-Men '97 S1 episode 9 ('Tolerance Is Extinction Part 2'), Magneto re-forms his mutant haven on Asteroid M and invites the X-Men. Rogue and Roberto (A:fox-anim-sunspot) join him against the X-Men until the episode 10 battle. The screen gives this following no group name. Should it be a stage, and under what name?
options: Add a stage for both under a name the owner picks (e.g. Magneto's Asteroid M, or 'The Acolytes' as in the TAS Asteroid M story), then 'The X-Men' again in S1
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia: 'He invites the X-Men to join him, which Rogue and Roberto do.' Marvel Database: 'Only Rogue and Sunspot took him up on his offer... much to the betrayal of the X-Men.'

owner_calls.question: X-Men: The Animated Series 'Slave Island' calls Cable a mercenary formerly employed by the Genoshan government (the Leader's regime) to capture mutants. Is that a past group (service in the Leader's forces) or a hire that doesn't count?
options: Add a past stage for the Genoshan government/Leader's army before Cable's Resistance (needs a name: the dataset's 'Genosha' is the later mutant nation)
owner_calls.evidence: Wikipedia: 'Cable, a mercenary formerly employed by the Genoshan government to capture mutants.' Marvel Database: 'Cable was once part of the Leader's army until he had discovered that the Leader was not truly a champion of democracy.'
